The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2.

That on 29.09.2022 at about 2.30 p.m. the petitioner was walking in Aster R.V.Hospital compound at J.P. Nagar, 1 st Phase, Bangalore from North to South direction, at that time, driver of car bearing registration No.KA-04/MZ-1346 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner from East to West direction and dashed the petitioner.
Due to the forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately he was shifted to Aster R.V.Hospital , Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and incurred sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards nourishment, medical expenses and other incidental charges.
4. It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 38 years and Machanic/Welding and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04/MZ-1346.
Hence, Jayanagara Traffic Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.139/2022.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.

6. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before this tribunal, remained absent,
hence she was placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further, admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing registration No.KA-04/MZ- 1346 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

sentences.text: This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

33. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injury:-

he might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an Kamalesh vs Shobha I.V on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104467147/

42. In such a situation, question of loss of future income does not arise all.

sentences.text: "The claimant has got disability to the extent of 46%.
The doctor has not spoken about the disability with regard to the whole body.

The claimant has permanent disability and thus has permanent diminution of his earning capacity, but he has been continued in the same employment without deduction of salary, the claimant is entitled for compensation for his handicap in the labor market.
In many cases of comparatively not serious injuries, though there is some permanent disability, the disability has no immediate adverse effect on his salary.
He may be getting the pre-accident salary.
However, such a man is at a disadvantage when compared with his co-workers in the labour market.

It may so happen that he continues to work with difficulty and gets the same salary but if there is reduction in the workforce by the employers, this worker with disability is likely to be sent off first."

43. On perusal of the above said decision, it is observed that, though the claimant is in a position to work physically after the accident as before, the after effects of the accident may make it more Kamalesh vs Shobha I.V on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104467147/
9 difficult for him to find work or to retain his work.
There would be some degree of physical handicap.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.

44. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued his job, he has to suffer with the said disability throughout his life and the eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to her disability.

Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.
On perusal of evidence of PW3 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

But, the petitioner has not placed any documents for consideration.
By taking neccessity of removal of implants, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
Due to the forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, Jayanagara Traffic Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.139/2022.
6. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before this tribunal, remained absent,
hence she was placed exparte.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that there is delay in lodging the complaint as the accident was taken place on 23.9.2022, but complaint was lodged on 29.9.2022.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Ultimately,
stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
In support of his contention relied the following decisions reported in;
1) ILR 2014 KAR 3336 between Branch Manager, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt.Kempamma & Others 2) ILR 2021 KAR 146 between The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Belagavi Vs. Smt.Reshama and Others 3) ILR 2009 KAR 2921 between Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. B.C. Kumar and Another 25.
26. On the contrary, at the time of arguments learned counsel for the petitioner relied the following decisions:
 1) 2018(1) KCCR 351 between  Sri.Yellappa Shivappa Sajali V/s Ashok  Ballappa Naik and another  2) 2021 ACJ 1309 between Vojje Mahankali  V/s M.Satyanarayana and another  3) 2020 ACJ 916 between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Shila Debi and others 4) Civil Appeal No.8174/2025 (arising out of SLP (C) No.8074/2025) between Suresh V/s Senthil B.
and another.
27. I have gone through the supra decisions the common principle laid down in the supra decisions are that, "where there is a dispute regarding manner of accident the hospital records particularly wound certificate is not a valid evidence without corroborating other evidence".
The insurance company must give rebuttal evidence in this regard.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 23.9.2022 at about 2.30 p.m. at Aster R.V.Hospital Compound, JP Nagar, 1st Phase, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MZ-1346 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?
From whom?
3) What order or award?
14. It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04/MZ- 1346 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
15.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
1) 2024 AAC 1121 between Aabid Khan Vs. Dinesh & Others 2) 2025 SCC 8074 between Suresh Vs. Senthil B. & Others 12. I have gone through the supra decisions, the common principle laid down in the supra decision are that, "doctor opinion regarding disability is considered as it is if there is no contra evidence".
13.
No doubt, the accident was taken place on 23.9.2022, but complaint was lodged on 29.9.2022.
Merely because there is some delay in lodging the complaint, it cannot be concluded that that the complaint is fictitious and filled with false information.
The delay is not a main ground to reject the claim petition.
The evidence of RW2 will not much helpful to prove the Ex.P14-discharge summary.
Even in the cross- examination of RW1 & RW3, respondent has not placed any supportive and reliable documents for consideration to believe its defenses against the case of the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 has not made an effort to examine either the driver of the offending vehicle or any independent eye witness to prove its defence.
Added to this,
the respondent No.2 has not challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
30. In the instant case, sketch and charge sheet clearly reveals that car bearing registration No.KA-04-MZ-1346 is involved in the accident.
Apart from this, Ex.P31-MLC clearly shows the history of accident as "road traffic accident pedestrian vs. four wheeler around 2.30 p.m.
(23.9.2022)".
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
After the accident he did not come to work.
But not placed any documents to show that due to the accidental injuries petitioner has not attended his duty.
From this, it is clear that the petitioner has continued his service.
42. In such a situation, question of loss of future income does not arise all.
Hence, I relied the decision reported in, ILR 2015 KAR 167 in between Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others, it was observed,
that.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.
44. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued his job, he has to suffer with the said disability throughout his life and the eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to her disability.
Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.
As per the records, the policy was valid from 30.6.2021 to 29.6.2024.
The alleged accident was taken place on 23.9.2022.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

10 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.Future
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,46,960/- (Rupees three lakhs forty six thousand nine hundred and sixty only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.3,46,960/- (Rupees  three lakhs forty six thousand nine hundred and sixty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.

Draw award accordingly.
